en: 6. Saṅkhāra Yamaka 6.2 Pavattivāra 6.2.3.
Uppādanirodhavāra (The Chapter on Arising and Cessation)
6.2.3.1 Present Section (Paccuppannavāra) 6.2.3.1.1 Positive Person (Anulomapuggala) Does bodily formation (kāyasaṅkhāra) arise for that person for whom verbal formation (vacīsaṅkhāra) ceases? No.
Or, for whom verbal formation ceases, does bodily formation arise for that person? No.
For whom bodily formation arises, does mental formation cease for that person? No.
Or, for whom mental formation ceases, does bodily formation arise for that person? No.
Does the mental formation cease for that person for whom the verbal formation arises? No.
Or conversely …pe… ? No. 6.2.3.1.2.
Positive Plane (Anuloma-okāsa).
Where bodily formation arises, does verbal formation cease there?
In the second jhāna and the third jhāna, it does not...
[and so on] (for other "wherever" cases, it is the same).
6.2.3.1.3. Positive Person-Space (Anuloma-puggalokāsa):
For whom, where, does the bodily formation (kāyasaṅkhāra) arise? …pe… (The "for whom" [yassaka] and "for whom, where" [yassayattha] sections are identical.)
6.2.3.1.4. Negative Person (Paccanīka-puggala) For whom bodily formation does not arise, for that person does verbal formation not cease?
At the moment of the dissolution of applied thought and sustained thought, for them bodily formation does not arise, but for them verbal formation [does] not [cease].

It does not cease. For those at the moment of arising of consciousness without inhalation and exhalation, for those at the moment of dissolution of consciousness without initial application and sustained application,
and for those who have attained cessation or are non-percipient beings, neither the bodily formation arises nor does the verbal formation cease.
Or rather, for whom verbal formation does not cease, for that person does bodily formation not arise?
At the moment of arising of inhalation and exhalation, for them verbal formation does not cease, yet it is not the case that bodily formation does not arise for them.
At the moment of arising of consciousness without inhalation and exhalation, and at the moment of arising of consciousness without applied thought and sustained thought...
At the moment of dissolution, for those who have attained cessation and for non-percipient beings,
verbal formation does not cease and bodily formation does not arise. For whom bodily formation does not arise, does mental formation not cease?
In all [beings] at the moment of the cessation of consciousness, bodily formation does not arise, yet mental formation does not cease for them.
For those without inhalation and exhalation— at the moment of the arising of consciousness, for those who have attained cessation, and for non-percipient beings—
neither bodily formation arises nor does mental formation cease.
Or rather: for whom mental formation does not cease, for that person does bodily formation not arise?
At the moment of arising of inhalation and exhalation, for them mental formation does not cease, yet for them bodily formation does not fail to arise.
[This is not the case] at the moment of arising of consciousness without inhalation and exhalation, nor for those who have attained cessation, nor for non-percipient beings.
For them, neither does the mental formation cease nor does the bodily formation arise.
Does the mental formation not cease for one in whom the verbal formation does not arise?
For all [beings] at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, the verbal formation does not arise for them, but the mental formation does not [cease] for them.

It does not cease. For those without applied thought and sustained thought—at the moment of the arising of consciousness, for those who have attained cessation, and for non-percipient beings—neither verbal formation arises nor does mental formation cease.
Or conversely, for whomsoever mental formation does not cease, does verbal formation not arise for them?
At the moment of the arising of applied thought and sustained thought, their mental formation does not cease, yet verbal formation does not fail to arise for them.
At the moment of the arising of consciousness without applied thought and sustained thought, for those who have attained cessation and for non-percipient beings,
neither mental formation nor verbal formation arises or ceases.
6.2.3.1.5. Negative Plane (Paccanīka-okāsa):
Where bodily formation does not arise …pe… 6.2.3.1.6.
Negative Person-Plane (Paccanīka-puggalokāsa)
For whom, where, the bodily formation does not arise … [etc.
… (The "for whom" and "where" sections are identical; however, in the "for whom and where" section, the phrase "those who have attained cessation" is not applicable.
6.2.3.2. Past Section.
6.2.3.2.1. Positive Person (Anulomapuggala) For whom bodily formation had arisen, for that person had verbal formation ceased? Yes.
(The past questions in the section on arising, the section on cessation, and the section on both arising and cessation should be expanded in the same manner.)
6.2.3.3. Future Section (Anāgatavāra) 6.2.3.3.1.
Positive Person (Anulomapuggala) For whom bodily formation (kāyasaṅkhāra) will arise, for that person will verbal formation (vacīsaṅkhāra) cease? Yes.
Or, for whomsoever verbal formation will cease, will bodily formation arise for that person?

At the moment of arising of the final consciousness of those in the sense-sphere realm; for that consciousness immediately after which the final consciousness of those in the sense-sphere realm will arise;
for those in the fine-material sphere and the immaterial sphere who are in their final existence; and for those [who will arise] in the fine-material sphere...
For those who, having been reborn in the formless realm, will attain final nibbāna there, at the moment of their death, verbal formation will cease,
but bodily formation will not arise for them. For others, however, both verbal formation will cease and bodily formation will arise.
For whom bodily formation will arise, for that one will mental formation cease? Yes.
Or rather, for whom mental formation will cease, for that one will bodily formation arise?

At the moment of the arising of the final consciousness of those in the sense-sphere realm, and for that consciousness immediately after which [there arises] another consciousness of those in the sense-sphere realm...

For those for whom the final consciousness will arise— namely, those in the fine-material sphere or the immaterial sphere who are destined for their final existence, and those who, having been reborn in the fine-material or immaterial sphere,
will attain *parinibbāna* at the moment of death— the mental formation (*cittasaṅkhāra*) will cease,
but the bodily formation (*kāyasaṅkhāra*) will not arise for them. For others, however, both the mental formation and [the bodily formation] will cease.
And the bodily formation will arise.
For whom verbal formation will arise, for that person will mental formation cease? Yes.
Or rather, for whom mental formation will cease, for that person will verbal formation arise?
At the moment of arising of the final consciousness, for those whose final consciousness— which is without applied thought and sustained thought—
will arise immediately after that consciousness, mental formation will cease, but vocal formation will not arise for them. For others, however,
both mental formation will cease and vocal formation will arise.
6.2.3.3.2. Positive Section (Anuloma-okāsa):
Where bodily formation will arise … [etc.
… 6.2.3.3.3. Positive Section on Persons and Bases (Anuloma-puggalokāsa)
For whom and where bodily formation will arise, for them and there will verbal formation cease?
For those who have attained the second jhāna or the third jhāna, bodily formation will arise there, but verbal formation will not cease for them there.
For those who have attained the first jhāna and for those of the sense-sphere realm...
In those [beings], both the bodily formation will arise and the verbal formation will cease there.
Or rather, for whomsoever the verbal formation will cease at a certain place, will the bodily formation arise for that person at that same place?

At the moment of the arising of the final consciousness of those in the sense-sphere realm, and for whichever consciousness immediately follows [that final consciousness] in those of the sense-sphere realm...
For those in the fine-material sphere and the immaterial sphere whose final consciousness is about to arise,

verbal formation will cease there, but bodily formation will not arise there for them. For those who have attained the first jhāna and for others in the sense-sphere, both verbal formation and bodily formation will cease and arise there respectively.
For whomsoever bodily formation will arise at a certain place, for that person mental formation will cease at that place? Yes.
Or rather, for whomsoever mental formation will cease at a certain place, for that person bodily formation will arise at that place?

At the moment of the arising of the final consciousness of those in the sense-sphere realm, and for that consciousness immediately after which [a new consciousness] arises for those in the sense-sphere realm...
For those who have attained the fourth jhāna— whether belonging to the fine-material sphere (*rūpāvacara*) or the immaterial sphere (*arūpāvacara*)—
the mental formation (*cittasaṅkhāra*) will cease there at their final consciousness, but the bodily formation (*kāyasaṅkhāra*) will not arise there for them.
For those who have attained the first, second, or third jhāna, and for others belonging to the sense-sphere (*kāmāvacara*), [the same applies].
In that case, mental formation will cease and bodily formation will arise.
For whomsoever verbal formation will arise in a certain place, for that person mental formation will cease in that same place? Yes.
Or conversely, for whomsoever mental formation will cease in a certain place, for that person verbal formation will arise in that same place?

At the moment of arising of the final consciousness, for those who have attained the second jhāna, the third jhāna, or the fourth jhāna— the final consciousness of which will arise immediately after [this moment]—
therein the mental formation (cittasaṅkhāra) will cease, but the verbal formation (vacīsaṅkhāra) will not arise for them there. [This applies to] the first jhāna.

For those who have attained [meditative absorption], for others belonging to the sense-sphere (*kāmāvacara*), the fine-material sphere (*rūpāvacara*), and the immaterial sphere (*arūpāvacara*), there the mental formation (*cittasaṅkhāra*) will cease and the verbal formation (*vacīsaṅkhāra*) will arise.
6.2.3.3.4. Negative Person (Paccanīkapuggala).
For whom bodily formation will not arise, for that person will verbal formation not cease?
[It will not] for those in the final moment of consciousness of the sense-sphere, for that consciousness immediately after which the final consciousness of the sense-sphere will arise,
for those in the fine-material sphere or the immaterial sphere who are in their final existence, and for those in the fine-material sphere...
For those who will attain final nibbāna after being reborn in the formless realm, at the moment of their death, bodily formation will not arise,
but it is not the case that vocal formation will not cease. [This is true] at the moment of the cessation of the final consciousness accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought,

for those possessing the final consciousness without applied thought and sustained thought, and for that consciousness immediately preceding the final consciousness without applied thought and sustained thought.
Will bodily formation not arise for them and vocal formation not cease?
Or, conversely …? Yes.
For whom bodily formation will not arise, will mental formation not cease for them?

At the moment of arising of the final consciousness of those in the sense-sphere realm; for those whose consciousness immediately following it will give rise to the final consciousness of the sense-sphere realm;

for those final-existence beings in the fine-material and immaterial realms; and for those who, having been reborn in the fine-material or immaterial realms, will attain final Nibbāna—when they are passing away, the bodily formation (kāya-saṅkhāra) will not arise in them.
And yet, their mental formation will not cease. At the moment of the dissolution of the final consciousness, for them, both bodily formation will not arise and mental formation will not cease.
Or, for whomsoever...? Yes.
For whom verbal formation will not arise, for them mental formation will not cease?

At the moment of arising of the final consciousness, and for those whose final consciousness— immediately following which a final consciousness without applied thought and sustained thought will arise—
their verbal formation will not arise, but it is not the case that their mental formation will not cease.
At the moment of the cessation of the final consciousness, for those [beings], verbal formation will not arise and mental formation will not cease.
Or, for whom...? Yes, it is so. 6.2.3.3.5.
Negative Plane (Paccanīka-okāsa)
Where bodily formation will not arise … [as above] … 6.2.3.3.6.
Negative Person-Location (Paccanīka-Puggalokāsa):
For whom, where bodily formation will not arise, for that person there, will verbal formation not cease?

At the moment of arising of the final consciousness of those belonging to the sense sphere (*kāmāvacara*), and for those whose consciousness immediately following it will give rise to the final consciousness of the sense sphere, or to the fine-material sphere (*rūpāvacara*), or to the immaterial sphere (*arūpāvacara*), bodily formation (*kāyasaṅkhāra*) will not arise therein;
yet, for them, vocal formation (*vacīsaṅkhāra*) will not fail to cease therein. [This applies] to the final consciousness accompanied by initial and sustained application (*savitakka-savicāra*).

At the moment of dissolution, for those possessing the final consciousness that is without initial application and without sustained application, for those whose next consciousness immediately following will arise as the final consciousness without initial application and without sustained application,
for those who have attained the fourth jhāna, and for non-percipient beings— among these,
neither the bodily formation nor the verbal formation will arise, and the verbal formation will not cease.
Or again, for whomsoever verbal formation will not cease at a certain place, will bodily formation not arise for them there?
For those who have attained the second jhāna or the third jhāna, verbal formation will not cease there, yet bodily formation will not fail to arise for them there.
[This is so] for one’s final consciousness accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought.

At the moment of dissolution, for those possessing the final consciousness that is without initial application and sustained application, for those whose final consciousness immediately following this will arise as one without initial application and sustained application,
for those who have attained the fourth jhāna, and for non-percipient beings— among these,
neither verbal formation nor bodily formation will cease, nor will bodily formation arise.
For whom, where bodily formation will not arise, for that person there will body formation cease?
At the moment of arising of the final consciousness of those in the sense sphere; for that consciousness immediately after which the final consciousness of the sense sphere will arise;
and for those who have attained the fourth jhāna, whether belonging to the fine-material sphere or the immaterial sphere.
For them, bodily formation will not arise there, but mental formation will not cease for them there.
At the moment of the dissolution of the final consciousness, and for non-percipient beings, both bodily formation and mental formation will neither arise nor cease there.
Or for whom, at whatever [place]...? Yes.
For whom, at whatever [place], verbal formation will not arise, for that person, at that place, will mental formation not cease?
At the moment of arising of the final consciousness, and for that consciousness immediately after which the final consciousness is without initial application and sustained application.
For those who have attained the second jhāna, the third jhāna, or the fourth jhāna, verbal formation will not arise there,
but mental formation will not fail to cease there for them. At the moment of the cessation of the final consciousness,
and for non-percipient beings, both verbal formation and mental formation will not arise there.
And it will not cease.
Or, for whomsoever, wherever …pe…? Yes.
6.2.3.4. Section on the Present and the Past.
6.2.3.4.1. Positive Person (Anulomapuggala) For whom bodily formation arises, for that person did verbal formation cease? Yes.
Or rather, for whom verbal formation had ceased, for that person does bodily formation arise?
In all [beings] at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, in those without inhalation and exhalation at the moment of the arising of consciousness,
and in those who have attained cessation or are non-percipient beings, verbal formation has ceased, but bodily formation does not arise for them.
At the moment of the arising of inhalation and exhalation, for them both verbal formation has ceased and bodily formation arises.

(Just as in the section on Arising, the questions concerning the present and the past were analyzed both in direct order and in reverse order, so too in the section on Arising and Cessation, the questions concerning the present and the past are to be analyzed both in direct order and in reverse order. 6.2.3.5.
Section on the Present and the Future. 6.2.3.5.1.
Direct Order: Person.
For whom bodily formation arises, for that person will verbal formation cease? Yes.
Or rather, for whom verbal formation will cease, for that person does bodily formation arise?

[It does not arise] for all at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, for those without inhalation and exhalation at the moment of the arising of consciousness, and for those who have attained cessation.
For non-percipient beings, verbal formation will cease, but bodily formation does not arise for them.
At the moment of the arising of inhalation and exhalation, verbal formation will cease and bodily formation also arises for them.
For one in whom bodily formation arises, will mental formation cease? Yes.
Or again, for whom mental formation will cease, for that person does bodily formation arise?
For all those at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, for those at the moment of the arising of consciousness when there is no inhalation or exhalation,
and for those who have entered the attainment of cessation or are non-percipient beings— mental formation will cease for them, but bodily formation does not arise for them.
At the moment of the arising of inhalation and exhalation, both mental formation (cittasaṅkhāra) will cease and bodily formation (kāyasaṅkhāra) arises.
For whom verbal formation (vacīsaṅkhāra) arises, for that person will mental formation cease? Yes.
Or conversely, for whom mental formation will cease, for that person does verbal formation arise?

In all [beings] at the moment of the cessation of consciousness, at the moment of the arising of consciousness without initial and sustained application, in those who have attained the attainment of cessation,
and in non-percipient beings— the mental formation will cease, but the verbal formation does not arise for them.
At the moment of the arising of initial and sustained application, for them both the mental formation will cease and the verbal formation arises.
6.2.3.5.2. Positive Plane (Anuloma-okāsa):
Where bodily formation arises … [etc.
… 6.2.3.5.3. Positive Person-Plane (Anuloma-puggalokāsa)
For whom and where bodily formation arises, for that person and in that place will verbal formation cease?

For those who have attained the second jhāna or the third jhāna at the moment of the arising of inhalation and exhalation, bodily formation arises there, but verbal formation will not cease there for them. [In the case of] the first jhāna...
In those who have attained [meditative absorption] and in those in the sensuous sphere at the moment of the arising of inhalation and exhalation,
both bodily formation and verbal formation arise there. Or rather,
for whomsoever verbal formation will cease in a certain place, does bodily formation arise for that person in that same place?
For those who have attained the first jhāna, at the moment of the dissolution of in-breaths and out-breaths belonging to the sense-sphere,
and for those very same persons at the moment of the arising of consciousness without in-breaths and out-breaths, as well as for those of the fine-material sphere and the immaterial sphere—
at these times and in these cases, verbal formation will cease, but bodily formation does not arise for them there. [Regarding] the first jhāna...

In those who have attained [meditative absorption] and in those in the sensuous sphere at the moment of the arising of inhalation and exhalation, verbal formation will cease and bodily formation arises therein.
For whomsoever bodily formation arises therein, will mental formation cease therein for that person? Yes.
Or, for whomsoever mental formation will cease at a certain place, does bodily formation arise for them there?

For all [beings] at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, and for those at the moment of the arising of consciousness when breath-in and breath-out are absent, mental formation will cease there, but bodily formation does not arise for them there. [This is so] regarding breath-in and breath-out.
At the moment of arising, for those [beings], mental formation will cease and bodily formation arises therein.
For whomsoever vocal formation arises therein, will mental formation cease therein for that person? Yes.
Or conversely, for whomsoever mental formation will cease therein, does vocal formation arise therein for that person?
For all [beings] at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, and for those at the moment of the arising of consciousness when it is devoid of initial application and sustained application,

mental formation will cease there, but vocal formation does not arise there for them. For those at the moment of the arising of initial application and sustained application, mental formation will cease there and vocal formation also arises there.
6.2.3.5.4. Negative Person (Paccanīka-puggala) For whom bodily formation does not arise, for that person will vocal formation not cease?

[It will not] for all [beings] at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, for those without inhalation and exhalation at the moment of the arising of consciousness, and for those who have attained cessation.
For non-percipient beings, bodily formation does not arise; yet, for them, verbal formation will not cease.

At the moment of the dissolution of the final consciousness accompanied by initial and sustained application, for those possessing the final consciousness without initial or sustained application, and for those for whom the final consciousness without initial or sustained application will arise immediately after the present consciousness—their bodily formation...
And [it is such that] bodily formation does not arise and verbal formation will not cease.
Or, for whomsoever verbal formation will not cease, for him does bodily formation not arise? Yes.
For whomsoever bodily formation does not arise, for him will mental formation not cease?

In all [beings] at the moment of the cessation of consciousness, at the moment of the arising of consciousness when there is no inhalation or exhalation, and in those who have attained the attainment of cessation and non-percipient beings, bodily formation does not arise; yet, for them, mental formation will not fail to cease.
At the moment of the cessation of the final consciousness, for them, both bodily formation does not arise and mental formation will not cease.
Or again: For whom mental formation will not cease, for that person does bodily formation not arise? Yes.
For whom verbal formation does not arise, for that person will mental formation not cease?
[It will not cease] for all at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, for those without applied thought and sustained thought, and for those who have entered the attainment of cessation.
For non-percipient beings, verbal formation does not arise, yet mental formation will not cease for them.
At the moment of the dissolution of the final consciousness, for them both verbal formation does not arise and mental formation will not cease.
Or rather, for whomsoever mental formation will not cease, for him verbal formation does not arise? Yes.
6.2.3.5.5. Negative Plane (Paccanīka-okāsa):
Where bodily formation does not arise …pe… 6.2.3.5.6.
Negative Person-Plane (Paccanīka-puggalokāsa)
For whom and where bodily formation does not arise, for that person and in that place will verbal formation not cease?
[It will not cease] for those who have attained the first jhāna, for those in the sense-sphere at the moment of the dissolution of inhalation and exhalation,

for those same persons at the moment of the arising of consciousness without inhalation and exhalation, and for those in the fine-material and immaterial spheres— at these, for them, [verbal formation will not cease].

Bodily formation does not arise, yet for them, vocal formation will not cease there. This is the case at the moment of dissolution of the final consciousness accompanied by initial and sustained application;

for those possessing the final consciousness without initial or sustained application; for one whose consciousness immediately follows which the final consciousness without initial or sustained application will arise;
for those who have attained the second jhāna or the third jhāna; and for those during inhalation and exhalation.
At the moment of dissolution of those very same [states], at the moment of arising of consciousness for those who have attained the fourth jhāna without inhalation and exhalation,
and for non-percipient beings— therein, the bodily formation does not arise and the verbal formation will not cease.
Or again, for whomsoever bodily formation does not arise at a certain place where verbal formation will not cease, is it the case that for them bodily formation does not arise there?

For those who have attained the second jhāna or the third jhāna at the moment of the arising of inhalation and exhalation, verbal formation will not cease there, yet bodily formation does not fail to arise there. [This is so] for the final consciousness accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought (*savitakka-savicāra*).

At the moment of dissolution for those possessing the final consciousness free from initial application and sustained application; for those whose final consciousness free from initial application and sustained application will arise immediately after this consciousness;
for those who have attained the second jhāna or the third jhāna at the moment of dissolution of inhalation and exhalation;
and for those same persons, at the moment of arising of consciousness without inhalation and exhalation during the fourth jhāna.
For those who have attained [meditative absorption] and for non-percipient beings, neither verbal formation nor bodily formation will cease there.
For whomsoever bodily formation does not arise there, will mental formation not cease there for them?

For all [beings] at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, and for those at the moment of the arising of consciousness when breath-in and breath-out are absent, [mental formation will not cease] there for them.
Bodily formation does not arise, but mental formation will not cease for them there either. At the moment of the cessation of the final consciousness,
and for non-percipient beings, neither bodily formation nor mental formation arises or will cease there.
Or rather: For whomsoever mental formation will not cease at a certain place, for that person does bodily formation not arise there? Yes.
For whomsoever verbal formation does not arise at a certain place, for that person will mental formation not cease there?

[It will not] for all those at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, and for those at the moment of the arising of consciousness without initial application and sustained application; for them, it will not cease there.
Verbal formation does not arise, yet mental formation will not cease for them there. At the moment of the dissolution of the final consciousness,
and for non-percipient beings, neither verbal formation arises nor will mental formation cease for them there.
Or rather: For whomsoever mental formation will not cease at a certain place, for that person does verbal formation not arise there?
Yes. 6.2.3.6. Chapter on the Past and Future.
6.2.3.6.1. Positive Person.
For whom bodily formation has arisen, will verbal formation cease for them?

At the moment of dissolution of the final consciousness accompanied by initial application and sustained application; for those possessing the final consciousness without initial application and sustained application;

and for those whose final consciousness without initial application and sustained application will arise immediately after that consciousness—for these, bodily formation [has arisen, but verbal formation will not cease].
[In some cases] bodily formation had arisen for them, but vocal formation will not cease for them.
For others, however, both bodily formation had arisen and vocal formation will cease.
Or, for whomsoever vocal formation will cease, had bodily formation arisen for them? Yes.
For whom bodily formation had arisen, will mental formation cease for them?

At the moment of the cessation of the final consciousness, bodily formation had arisen for them, but mental formation will not cease for them. For others, both bodily formation had arisen and mental formation will cease.
Or, for whom mental formation will cease, had bodily formation arisen for them? Yes.

Just as in the section on cessation, the questions concerning the past and future— both in direct order and in reverse order— are to be analyzed without confusion in the same way in the section on arising and cessation;
it is similar to the section on cessation, there being no difference.
The Section on Arising and Cessation.
